Subject: Tuesday reading club – an update before the review

Dear Niamh,

I wanted to send you an update on the Tuesday reading club before the review meeting on Wednesday 18 November. There is good news about attendance, and there is also something I need to put right with you.

Since your email of 30 October about pausing the club from January, I’ve been thinking about the concerns you raised over low attendance and the increase in the hall insurance. I know those are real considerations. But I’d love you to have the latest figures before the meeting, because things have changed quite a bit.

We had five children most weeks in September, nine by mid-October, and fourteen last Tuesday, 3 November. It has taken time to build up since we started in September 2025, but the Tuesday session, from 3.30 to 4.45 in the upstairs meeting room at Knocknacarra library, is really finding its feet now. I’m thrilled to see it.

We’ve also had a very generous donation from Declan Moran at Salthill Book Nook: 120 books, mostly for the six-to-nine age group, with a good few as Gaeilge. It gives us a lovely choice for the children.

The numbers matter, of course, but there are smaller things happening that mean just as much to me. Two sisters from a Ukrainian family joined us in October, and the older girl now reads to her younger sister in English at the end of each session. One boy who wouldn’t open a book in September asked last week if he could take two home. After years in the classroom, those are still the moments that make my day.

I hope you might reconsider the January pause in light of this. I don’t imagine the insurance difficulty has disappeared, but it would be a terrible pity to stop just as the club is taking off. Is there a way we could keep it going and review attendance again after a further stretch?

The other matter is a conversation I had with Orla Keane from the Corrib Courier at the farmers’ market. I got carried away telling her about the club and said, “Come along any Tuesday.” She would now like to come on Tuesday 24 November with a photographer.

I was wrong not to check with you first, plain and simple, and I wanted you to hear it from me. I know that photographs of children require your sign-off and the parental consent forms. My invitation should not have got ahead of that process.

I’m very happy to ring Orla and put the visit on hold until you’ve decided whether it should go ahead. If you do agree, I can collect the consent forms myself and help with the arrangements under your direction. The coverage could be wonderful for the club, but only if it’s done properly.

Thank you for considering all of this before the meeting. I know you have more than our Tuesday group to look after, and I appreciate the work that goes into keeping these clubs running. I’m hopeful that the new numbers will give us a chance to carry on.

Warm wishes,

[Your name]
